column5: A number field E that is a totally imaginary quadratic extension of a totally real number field E+; complex conjugation is the nontrivial automorphism of E/E+ and commutes with every complex embedding.
column6: Number field; Totally real number field; Complex embedding of a number field

column5: A number field all of whose embeddings into C have image in R.
column6: Number field; Complex embedding of a number field

column1: Complex embedding of a number field
column5: A ring homomorphism from a number field E to C. A CM type is a choice of one embedding Phi_v from each pair of conjugate embeddings, i.e. one per infinite place.

column1: Infinite place of a number field
column5: An archimedean place of a number field E: an absolute value x -> |phi(x)| for a complex embedding phi, embeddings being identified with their conjugates. The absolute value used is the ordinary complex modulus (not squared at complex places). For a CM field of degree 2f there are f infinite places, all complex.
column6: Number field; Complex embedding of a number field; Place of a global field

column5: The ideal of O_E inverse to the codifferent {x in E : Tr(x O_E) in Z}. Its absolute norm is |disc E|. In this proof it is principal with a purely imaginary generator varpi.
column6: Number field; Ring of integers of a number field; Codifferent of a number field; Absolute norm of an ideal

column5: For a number field E of degree n, rd_E = |disc E|^(1/n). For a CM field with f infinite places, |disc E| = rd_E^(2f).
column6: Number field; Discriminant of a number field

column5: The determinant of the trace form on an integral basis of O_E.

column1: Finite adele ring of a number field
column5: The restricted product of the completions E_w over the finite places w with respect to the rings of integers; O-hat is the product of the local rings of integers, a compact open subring.
column6: Number field; Completion of a field at a place

column5: A nonzero left-invariant Radon measure on a locally compact group; unique up to a positive scalar.
The translation-invariant Borel measure on R^n giving the unit cube measure 1; on C it is the Lebesgue measure of R^2.

column1: Fundamental domain for a group action
column5: For a countable group Gamma acting measurably on a measure space, a (null-)measurable set F such that almost every point (here: every point) has exactly one translate gamma x in F. If the action preserves the measure, the integral of a nonnegative function f equals the integral over F of the sum of f over the orbit.

column1: Strong approximation for the additive group
column5: A number field E is dense in its ring of finite adeles (diagonal embedding).
column6: Finite adele ring of a number field

column5: A sesquilinear form h on a vector space over a field with involution satisfying h(y,x) = conj h(x,y); given in a basis by a matrix J with J* = J. An isometry is an invertible g with g* J g = J; the isometries form the unitary group U(J).
A two-dimensional hermitian space with a basis e, e* of isotropic vectors with h(e, e*) = 1.
A square matrix with ones on the diagonal and zeros below it; more generally, for a level function on the indices, a matrix g with g_ij = delta_ij whenever level(j) <= level(i). They form a group.
From vectors v_1..v_n of an inner product space, the orthogonal vectors w_a = v_a - sum_{b<a} <w_b,v_a>/|w_b|^2 w_b; the coefficients form an upper unitriangular matrix.
An element of a number field that is a root of a monic polynomial with integer coefficients. A nonzero algebraic integer has some archimedean absolute value >= 1 (its norm is a nonzero integer).
column6: Number field; Ring of integers of a number field

column1: Packing bound in a normed space
column5: In a real normed space of finite dimension d, points with pairwise distances at least m > 0 and norms at most R number at most (1 + 2R/m)^d (comparison of volumes of disjoint balls).
column6: Normed space; Dimension of a vector space

column5: The integral of a strongly measurable function with values in a Banach space; here with the convention that the integral of a non-integrable function is 0. It satisfies ||int f|| <= int ||f||.

column1: Mass of a genus of hermitian lattices
column5: For the standard hermitian lattice O_E^l over a CM field, the sum of 1/#(Gamma cap g K g^-1) over the double cosets Gamma g K of the finite adelic unitary group, K the stabiliser of the lattice and Gamma the rational unitary group. The mass formula (Siegel, Shimura) evaluates it; here only an approximate ratio formula for consecutive ranks is used.
column6: CM field; Hermitian form; Finite adele ring of a number field

column5: A continuous homomorphism from a locally compact abelian group (here the adeles or finite adeles of E) to the unit circle. The standard additive character psi of A_E is trivial on E; psi_f is its finite part; x -> psi_f(-x/varpi) makes O-hat self-dual when varpi generates the different.
column6: Adele ring of a number field; Different of a number field

column1: Adele ring of a number field
column5: The product of E tensor R with the finite adeles; E embeds diagonally as a discrete cocompact subring.
column6: Number field; Finite adele ring of a number field

column5: The group of units of the (finite) adele ring. An integral finite idele c has an index [O-hat : c O-hat], the inverse of the factor by which multiplication by c scales Haar measure.
column6: Finite adele ring of a number field

column5: For a definite unitary group H over a CM field: a function on H(A_f) with values in a finite-dimensional algebraic representation (here the Weyl module of weight kw), equivariant under H(E) on the left and invariant under an open subgroup (the level) on the right. Determined by its values at double coset representatives.
column6: CM field; Hermitian form; Finite adele ring of a number field; Double coset; Weyl module

column1: Automorphic form on an adelic group
column5: Here: a continuous function on G = G_infinity x G_f, left invariant under the rational points Gamma, right invariant under an open subgroup of G_f. A 'form of type e' is in addition bounded and fixed by right convolution over G_infinity with a kernel e (if e is integrable).
column6: Adele ring of a number field; Convolution on a locally compact group

column5: <F, F'> = integral over Gamma\G of conj(F) F' for the invariant quotient measure; conjugate-linear in the first variable as used here.
column6: Automorphic form on an adelic group; Quotient measure on a homogeneous space

column5: For a function B on G with suitable decay, the series sum over gamma in Gamma of B(gamma g); it is Gamma-invariant, and pairing it with an automorphic form unfolds to an integral over G.
column6: Automorphic form on an adelic group

column5: For a discrete subgroup Gamma of a unimodular group G and integrable F on G: the series sum_gamma F(gamma g) is integrable on Gamma\G and its integral is the integral of F over G. More generally integrals over a quotient are computed with a cutoff (a nonnegative measurable function whose Gamma-translates sum to 1).
column6: Quotient measure on a homogeneous space; Haar measure

column1: Quotient measure on a homogeneous space
column5: For a closed unimodular subgroup H of a unimodular locally compact group G, the G-invariant measure on H\G characterised by int_G f = int_{H\G} int_H f(hx) dh dx. In the Lean source it is realised as (cutoff) x (Haar measure of G).
column6: Haar measure; Unimodular locally compact group

column5: A locally compact group whose left Haar measures are right invariant.
Two left Haar measures on a locally compact group differ by a positive constant factor.
For s-finite measures and a nonnegative measurable function on a product, the double integral equals either iterated integral; sums of nonnegative terms may be exchanged with integrals.
For an integrable function on a product of s-finite measure spaces the integral equals the iterated integrals.
If measurable f_n converge pointwise and are dominated by an integrable function, the integrals converge; in particular a series with summable integrals of norms may be integrated term by term.

column1: Unitary group of a hermitian form
column5: For a hermitian matrix J over a ring with involution: the group U(J) of invertible g with g* J g = J. Related existing knowl: lie-groups/unitary-group (the compact U(n)).
An invertible linear map g with h(gx, gy) = h(x, y); in matrices g* J g = J.
For a matrix A over a ring with involution, A* has entries (A*)_ij = conj(A_ji).
The matrix (h(v_i, v_j)) of a sesquilinear form on a family of vectors.
A lattice over an integral ring R whose Gram matrix has entries in R and determinant a unit of R; then the lattice equals its dual, and an isometry k with k - 1 integral has integral inverse.
An element e of a ring with e e = e. In the finite adeles the idempotent of a set of places is 1 at those places and 0 elsewhere.
For subgroups A, B of a group G, a set A g B. The classes of the filling data are the double cosets U(X_0)(E)\U(X_0)(A_f)/K_source.
The kernel of reduction of an integral matrix group modulo an ideal (here: modulo the chosen places above M = p_0 p_1); equivalently the integral isometries k with M^-1 (k - 1) integral.
column6: Finite adele ring of a number field; Residue field

column5: The quotient of a local ring (here the ring of integers of the completion of E at a finite place w) by its maximal ideal; a finite field with N(w) elements.
For a unipotent algebraic group U over a number field E, U(E) is dense in U(A_f); here: for x in U(A_f) and any y, some rational u has y^-1 x^-1 u y in the principal congruence subgroup.
column6: Finite adele ring of a number field; Unitriangular matrix

column5: An irreducible unitary representation of a real reductive group (here U(p,q)) occurring as a subrepresentation of L^2(G); its matrix coefficients are square integrable. Parametrised by Harish-Chandra parameters.
column6: Unitary group of a hermitian form; Irreducible representation; Haar measure

column5: The regular infinitesimal character parameter lambda of a discrete series of U(p,q), a strictly decreasing sequence; the Lean source stores the doubled parameter l = 2 lambda (integers).
For a discrete series pi and Haar measure dg: the positive number d_pi with int |<pi(g)v,w>|^2 dg = |v|^2 |w|^2 / d_pi. The kernel e = d_pi conj(coefficient) is an idempotent under convolution.

column1: Bessel function of a discrete series
column5: A vector-valued function W on a unitary group G_1 transforming by a generic character under the unipotent radical U of a Bessel subgroup R = U H and by a representation of H = U(k); here obtained by integrating a discrete series coefficient over R against the character. Analogue of Whittaker/J-Bessel functions.
For an automorphic form y on U(V) and a form phi on the smaller unitary group H: the integral over [R] = R(F)\R(A), R = U H the Bessel subgroup, of psi_U(u) phi(h) y(uh).
column6: Automorphic form on an adelic group; Additive character

column5: The irreducible polynomial representation of GL_k attached to a partition (given by column counts kw); for a one-row partition of length a it is the a-th symmetric power. Its matrices in a standard basis are the Schur matrices.
Sym^a(V): the space of homogeneous polynomials of degree a in a basis of V; dimension binom(k + a - 1, a) for dim V = k.
For matrices M_v indexed by a finite set, the matrix on product index sets with entries prod_v M_v(i_v, j_v); it is multiplicative and acts factor by factor on product vectors.
The norm sup |Ax|/|x| of a matrix acting on Euclidean space.
A complex vector space with a positive definite hermitian form; Cauchy-Schwarz: |<x,y>| <= |x||y|.
For a measurable u >= 1 and i > 0: int u^-i dmu = int_1^infinity i R^(-i-1) mu{u <= R} dR.
The index of the stabiliser of a point equals the size of its orbit.

column1: General linear group over a finite field
column5: GL_n(F_q); it acts transitively on the q^n - 1 nonzero vectors.
The inverse of exp on the positive reals; log y <= y - 1, and log(1+y) >= 2y/(y+2) for y >= 0.
n! = product of 1..n; (l-1)! <= l^l.

Shimura's exact formula for the mass of the genus of a unimodular hermitian lattice; only the approximate ratio of masses in consecutive ranks is used: log(mass_{j+1}/mass_j) = f((j+1/2) log rd_E + log j! - (j+1) log 2 pi) up to 2/2^u, for j >= 4u+12 and 8f <= 2^u.
column6: Mass of a genus of hermitian lattices; Root discriminant

column5: For a hermitian form h, an isotropic vector x and a vector u orthogonal to x: the isometry y -> y + h(u,y) x - h(x,y)(u + s x) with s + conj(s) = h(u,u). Generates unipotent elements of unitary groups.
column6: Hermitian form; Isometry of a hermitian space

column5: An element of exact multiplicative order n. If a CM field contains a primitive 5040-th root of unity then its ring of integers contains tau with tau + conj(tau) = 1, and E/E+ is unramified at the finite places.
